column1: # AA GRID -- push the WINNING corner further: 150/180 epochs x eta_min {3e-4, 5e-4, 7e-4}
# WHAT WE ARE TRYING TO ACHIEVE OVERALL
# Predict a perturbation's effect in a cellular context where that perturbation was never
# measured, from a single control cell. Headline: split-half paired `pearson_delta` on the 611
# held-out HepG2 perturbations, 6,983-gene axis, cell-eval 0.6.0, uncalibrated.
# WHAT THIS GRID ANSWERS
# F-sched3 found the best arm at the EDGE of both axes with both margins still positive:
# `Y06` (Q02, 150 ep, eta_min 3e-4) = 0.4043, with 120->150 worth +0.0028 (5/5) at that floor
# and 3e-4 beating every lower floor at both lengths. An endpoint optimum is a range problem,
# not a finished tuning (F-loss3), so this grid extends BOTH edges one step:
#   * epochs 150 -> 180 (+30, the step size used throughout)
#   * eta_min 3e-4 -> 5e-4, 7e-4 (0.5x and 0.7x of lr; 1e-3 would be NO decay and is excluded)
# WHAT IS VARIED / HELD FIXED
# VARIED: epochs (150, 180) x eta_min (3e-4, 5e-4, 7e-4), minus the (150, 3e-4) cell, which is
#   `Y06` itself and is not re-run.
# HELD FIXED: the Q02 loss composition exactly as Y06 -- smooth_l1 + dcos 0.5 + delta_mag
#   0.01363 + latent MSE (delta_z) 0.0044, no VICReg, no dispersion terms, no recon split --
#   batch 2048, lr 1e-3, decoder_lr 1e-3, warmup 5, seed 42, arm s313 otherwise.
# ⚠️ eta_min APPROACHES lr. At 7e-4 with lr 1e-3 the cosine only ever decays to 0.7x peak, so
# these arms are close to a CONSTANT learning rate. That is the point -- it asks whether the
# gain attributed to "a high floor" is really "decay does not help this model at all" -- but it
# also means a divergent arm is a plausible outcome rather than a bug. Read grad_norm.
# HOW TO READ THE RESULT -- PRE-REGISTERED
# AA01 (180, 3e-4) > 0.4063 at 4-5/5  -> the epochs axis is STILL live past 150; keep stepping.
# AA01 ~ 0.4043                       -> 150 is the plateau AT THIS FLOOR.
# AA02/AA03 (5e-4, 7e-4) > AA01       -> the floor is still the binding axis and the optimum is
#                                        nearer a CONSTANT lr than a decayed one.
# AA04/AA05 > Y06 (0.4043)            -> the floor helps at the KNOWN-GOOD length too, so the
#                                        two axes are separable after all.
# monotone decline in eta_min         -> 3e-4 was the optimum and F-sched3's edge was the peak.
# any arm diverges (grad_norm blows)  -> the usable floor has an upper bound; report it as the
#                                        measured ceiling rather than a failed arm.
# ANCHORS -- test, uncalibrated, 5/5 splits
# ctrlcell -0.0018 · ctrlmean 0.0016 · meanpert 0.1324 · transfer 0.2323 · experimental 0.3722
# (mae 0.0215, ovl@N 0.0946, disc_l1 0.7288). Directions: pearson_delta UP · mae DOWN (ERROR) ·
# ovl@N UP · disc_l1 UP.
# COST: 180 ep ~= 2 h 30, 150 ep ~= 2 h 05 (41 s/epoch measured) -> 5 arms ~= 11 GPU-h train,
# plus 25 eval tasks at ~9 min on a %6 throttle (F-infra1) ~= 4 GPU-h.
